```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Supabase exposes PostgreSQL tables, views and functions through its REST
Data API. Use `oauth_db_supabase_api()` to query with each visitor's access
token; database grants and row-level security (RLS) decide which rows they
can read or change. No PostgreSQL driver is needed.

The client provides the same `select()`, `rpc()` and `request()` methods as
the [PostgREST client](postgrest.html). It supports hosted projects and
self-hosted deployments exposed through verified HTTPS, including custom
domains and reverse proxy paths. It does not provide a SQL connection or
clients for Storage, Realtime or the Management API.

## Configure Supabase sign-in

For people with accounts in your Supabase project, enable the project's
[OAuth 2.1 server](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/oauth-server/getting-started).
This feature is currently in beta. It requires an existing sign-in and
consent page in your Supabase application; the Shiny app redirects to it.

In **Authentication > OAuth Server**, enable the server, configure its
authorization path and register a client with the exact Shiny redirect URI,
`http://localhost:8100` for this example. A deployed app needs its own HTTPS
redirect URI. For a confidential client, select `client_secret_basic` and
save its secret. Public clients registered with authentication method `none`
can omit the secret. Both use PKCE.

Configure an asymmetric signing key, such as ES256 or RS256. The default
client requests `openid` and validates signed ID tokens through OIDC
discovery and JWKS. Supabase's legacy HS256 signing setup cannot issue
these OIDC ID tokens. See the
[signing key guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/signing-keys).

Save these values in your app's `.Renviron`:

```text
OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_KEY=sb_publishable_your-project-key
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-oauth-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-oauth-client-secret
```

Use the project base URL, without `/rest/v1` or `/auth/v1`. Get the
publishable key from the project's API keys settings. It identifies your
application and is separate from the OAuth client ID and secret. For a
public client, leave `OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET` empty. Restart R after editing
`.Renviron` and keep the file out of Git.

The Data API client sends the publishable key in `apikey` and the current
visitor access token in `Authorization: Bearer ...`. It waits for sign-in
before sending requests. A legacy `anon` JWT also works, including on
self-hosted projects using legacy API keys. The helper rejects
`sb_secret_...` and legacy `service_role` keys. See
[Supabase API keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys).

## Prepare a table with user permissions

Run this example in the Supabase SQL editor, or use an existing table with
the grants and RLS policies your app needs:

```sql
create table public.oauthdb_notes (
  id bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users(id),
  note text not null
);

alter table public.oauthdb_notes enable row level security;
revoke all on public.oauthdb_notes from anon, authenticated;
grant select on public.oauthdb_notes to authenticated;

create policy "Visitors read their own notes"
  on public.oauthdb_notes for select to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = owner_id);
```

Add rows in the SQL editor using the UUIDs of two existing project users as
`owner_id`. Sign in as each user to verify that they see only their own
rows. An empty result can mean that RLS allows no matching rows.

Supabase OAuth scopes such as `openid`, `profile` and `email` control identity
information, not table access. Apply grants and RLS to exposed tables. You
can also restrict a policy to your app with `auth.jwt() ->> 'client_id'`.
See [OAuth tokens and RLS](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/oauth-server/token-security).

## A complete Shiny app

Save this as `example.R`, then run `source("example.R")`:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

project_url <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_URL")
client <- oauth_db_supabase_client(
  url = project_url,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  supabase <- oauth_db_supabase_api(
    auth$connection,
    url = project_url,
    api_key = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_KEY")
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    supabase$select("oauthdb_notes", order = "id.asc", limit = 20L)
  })
}

runApp(shinyApp(ui, server), port = 8100, launch.browser = FALSE)

# Open http://localhost:8100 in your regular browser
```

`oauth_db_supabase_client()` discovers the project's `/auth/v1` OIDC issuer.
shinyOAuth handles the authorization-code flow, identity validation and
token renewal. Supabase issues refresh tokens without requiring an
`offline_access` scope. Calls to the Data API use the access token.

## Use an existing third-party identity provider

A project configured to trust a
[third-party provider](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/third-party/overview)
can use that provider's authorization directly. Register the Shiny app with
the provider and configure the JWT claims required by your Supabase
integration. A provider enabled only as a Supabase social-login option does
not establish direct Data API trust for that provider's tokens.

Replace the app's client with your existing shinyOAuth client, or pass
`provider` and `scopes` explicitly:

```{r external-client}
provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SUPABASE_ISSUER")
)
client <- oauth_db_supabase_client(
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  provider = provider,
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "email")
)
```

The Data API client stays the same. Native Supabase Auth uses UUID subjects
with `auth.uid()`; external providers may use other subject formats, so write
their policies against the appropriate verified JWT claims.

## Functions, schemas and writes

Use `schema = "reporting"` to select another schema exposed by the Data API.
The client sends `Accept-Profile` for reads and `Content-Profile` for writes.
The signed-in user's role still needs schema and object privileges.

```{r native-requests}
# Call an existing database function with the visitor's permissions.
total <- supabase$rpc("note_total", list(category = "work"))

# A write requires grants and an RLS policy permitting updates.
response <- supabase$request(
  "oauthdb_notes",
  method = "PATCH",
  query = list(id = "eq.42"),
  body = list(note = "Reviewed"),
  prefer = "return=representation",
  raw = TRUE
)
```

`select()` returns one page; use `limit`, `offset` and a deterministic order
to fetch more. The [PostgREST guide](postgrest.html) covers filters, embedded
resources, counts and result types. The project must expose a function
before `rpc()` can call it; this client does not execute arbitrary SQL.

GET and HEAD retry once after HTTP 401 with a renewed visitor token.
Writes and POST function calls never retry automatically. Requests reject
redirects and discard responses after account changes, sign-out or permission
loss. The project key stays attached to the client when a visitor changes
accounts.
